rows.text: Gishath does not cast anything. When it connects, it reveals one card per point of damage and puts every Dinosaur among them straight onto the battlefield. Every extra point of damage is another card revealed — so DOUBLE STRIKE on Gishath means two separate reveals, and a second creature carrying Gishath's trigger means two more. Nothing it puts in was cast, which matters for exactly one card here: Zacama only untaps your lands when it is cast.

rows.name: Gishath, Sun's Avatar
rows.text: 7/6 vigilance, trample and haste for eight. It attacks the turn it lands, it stays back as a blocker, and with 28 Dinosaurs in the ninety-nine a seven-card reveal averages two free ones.

rows.name: Devil Dinosaur
rows.text: other Dinosaurs get +1/+1 and HEXPROOF — and Gishath is a Dinosaur. Four mana makes your commander untargetable and pushes its hit to eight cards.

rows.name: Regal Imperiosaur
rows.text: the second anthem, three mana for a 5/4. With both out Gishath hits for nine and reveals nine cards.

rows.name: Sunfrill Imitator
rows.text: when it attacks, it becomes a copy of another Dinosaur you control — point it at Gishath and you have a second 7/6 trampler with the same reveal trigger. Its name stays Sunfrill Imitator, so the legend rule never applies. Three mana for a second Gishath every combat.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: shroud for the turn you cannot afford to lose Gishath to a removal spell.

rows.name: Cavern of Souls
rows.text: name Dinosaur and Gishath cannot be countered.

rows.name: Rhythm of the Wild
rows.text: no creature spell of yours can be countered, and every nontoken creature enters with haste or a counter.
Gishath's trigger fires in every combat damage step where it damages a player, and first-strike damage and regular damage are two steps. The first reveal resolves before the second damage step.

rows.name: Goring Ceratops
rows.text: when it attacks, every other creature you control gains double strike — so Ceratops has to be attacking alongside Gishath. Revealing it mid-combat is too late for this combat.

rows.name: Boros Charm
rows.text: two mana for double strike on Gishath at instant speed, after blockers are declared.

rows.name: Akroma's Will
rows.text: with your commander out you take both halves — flying and double strike for two reveals, plus indestructible and protection from every colour. Coloured creatures cannot block it; colourless ones still can.

rows.name: Rogue's Passage
rows.text: {4} and Gishath cannot be blocked. The simplest way to guarantee the trigger.

rows.name: Triceraton Commander
rows.text: when it attacks, every other Dinosaur you control gets +1/+1 and FLYING. Revealed with X of zero it makes no tokens, but the attack trigger does not care about X — next turn it makes the whole team fly.

rows.name: Ghalta the Unstoppable
rows.text: costs {X} less where X is your biggest creature's power, so with Gishath out it is {1}{G}. Every other creature you control gains trample.

rows.name: Garruk's Uprising
rows.text: trample for the whole team, and a card for every creature with power four or more that enters — nearly every Dinosaur here.

rows.name: Hunting Velociraptor
rows.text: once any Dinosaur deals combat damage to a player, every Dinosaur spell you cast that turn has prowl {2}{R}. Gishath connects, and in your second main phase Polyraptor, Apex Altisaur and Etali each cost three.

rows.name: Selvala, Heart of the Wilds
rows.text: {G} and a tap for X mana in any colours, where X is your biggest creature's power — seven with Gishath out. Its draw clause is symmetrical: whoever plays the new biggest creature may draw.

rows.name: Polyraptor
rows.text: whenever it is dealt damage, it makes a token copy of itself. Every copy has the same ability.

rows.name: Forerunner of the Empire
rows.text: whenever a Dinosaur enters, it MAY deal 1 damage to every creature. Each ping makes every Polyraptor copy itself, and each copy entering lets Forerunner ping again. Forerunner also puts a Dinosaur from your library on top when it enters, so it finds Polyraptor on its own.

Unprotected, Forerunner is a 1/3 and dies to its own third ping. The best line gives exactly eight Polyraptors: when the second ping produces two copies, let the first copy enter, DECLINE the ping it offers, let the second copy enter, then take the third ping with four Polyraptors on the battlefield.

Make Forerunner indestructible before you start and there is no ceiling: Heroic Intervention, Boros Charm's second mode, or cycling Agonasaur Rex onto it. Akroma's Will also works, but only if it resolves BEFORE Polyraptor enters — its protection from red would stop Forerunner's pings reaching anything already on the battlefield.
Stop an unbounded loop well before your library runs low. Vaultborn Tyrant and Garruk's Uprising draw a card for every Polyraptor copy, and those draws are not optional.

rows.name: Regisaur Alpha
rows.text: every other Dinosaur has haste, so the army attacks the turn it is made. Eight hasty 5/5s is forty damage on an open board — one player dead, often two with the anthems, but not automatically the table.

rows.name: Terror of the Peaks
rows.text: each Polyraptor entering deals its power to any target, so the eight-Polyraptor line is forty damage before combat. Not a Dinosaur, but the best payoff in the deck.

rows.name: Wrathful Raptors
rows.text: whenever a Dinosaur you control is dealt damage, it deals that much to a target that isn't a Dinosaur. Every ping becomes a burn spell per Dinosaur. It CANNOT target Polyraptor, so it is a payoff, never a way to start the loop.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: thirteen damage to every creature, usually for one or two mana. With Wrathful Raptors out, every Dinosaur you control then deals thirteen damage to a target of your choice — four Dinosaurs is fifty-two damage to spread across the table. Each Polyraptor also leaves a fresh copy behind. Without Wrathful it is a reset that costs you your board too.

Marauding Raptor is deliberately not in this deck. Its Polyraptor loop is mandatory, so it draws the game unless someone breaks it or a payoff is already out, and its entry damage kills your own mana creatures.

guide.title: What the reveal wants to hit

rows.name: Etali, Primal Conqueror
rows.text: each player exiles cards until they hit a nonland, and you cast every one of them free. Put in by Gishath, it still triggers.

cards.name: Etali, Primal Conqueror // Etali, Primal Sickness

rows.name: Apex Altisaur
rows.text: fights a creature when it enters, and fights again every time it is dealt damage. On a single reveal it usually clears most of an opponent's board — and with Wrathful Raptors out, every fight also burns a face.

rows.name: Trumpeting Carnosaur
rows.text: discover 5 on entry — another free spell on top of the free creature.

rows.name: Earthshaker Dreadmaw
rows.text: a card for every other Dinosaur you control. Off a Gishath hit that is often five or more.

rows.name: Vaultborn Tyrant
rows.text: three life and a card whenever it or any creature with power four or more enters, and it comes back as an artifact copy the first time it dies.

rows.name: Pantlaza, Sun-Favored
rows.text: once per turn, a Dinosaur entering discovers X, where X is its toughness. A Gishath hit is a free spell as well as free creatures.

rows.name: Ghalta, Stampede Tyrant

rows.name: Etali, Primal Storm

rows.name: Dinosaurs on a Spaceship
rows.text: other Dinosaurs get +1/+1, vigilance and trample. Suspend it on turn five and it also makes a 2/2 flying, hasty Dinosaur on each of the next four upkeeps.

rows.name: Agonasaur Rex
rows.text: an 8/8 trampler for five, or cycle it for a card and make any creature indestructible with two +1/+1 counters.

rows.name: Birds of Paradise

rows.name: Elvish Mystic

rows.name: Kinjalli's Caller
rows.text: every Dinosaur costs one less, and it is a 0/3 so it survives the Forerunner loop's first two pings.

rows.name: Otepec Huntmaster
rows.text: the second Dinosaur discount, and it taps to give any Dinosaur haste. With both reducers out, Gishath costs six.

rows.name: Hulking Raptor
rows.text: two green mana at the beginning of the first main phase of each of your turns, on a warded 5/3.

rows.name: Topiary Stomper

rows.name: Ranging Raptors
rows.text: a basic land every time it is dealt damage — including every Forerunner ping.

rows.name: Regal Behemoth
rows.text: makes you the monarch, and while you are, every land taps for an extra mana.

rows.text: costs {X} less for your biggest creature's power — with Gishath out it is two green mana. Then every NONTOKEN creature that enters under your control gets a counter and draws you a card. Polyraptor copies are tokens and do not.

rows.name: Sylvan Library

rows.name: Curious Altisaur
rows.text: a card for every Dinosaur that deals combat damage to a player.

rows.name: Mosswort Bridge
rows.text: once your creatures total ten power — Gishath plus almost anything — it plays the hidden card free.

rows.name: Swords to Plowshares

rows.text: a land that becomes four damage to an attacker, and costs less for every legend you control.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a mana creature or a land-fetch spell and at least three lands. Gishath costs eight; the deck is at its best when it lands on turn four or five, and every card in the opener should be pulling toward that.
Cast Gishath before your other big threats. It is the engine — one connection puts free Dinosaurs in, which beats hard-casting one of them, and Hunting Velociraptor makes the rest cheap afterwards.
Play Devil Dinosaur or Rhythm of the Wild before Gishath if you can. Hexproof and "can't be countered" answer the two ways an eight-drop commander gets stopped.
Attack with Sunfrill Imitator alongside Gishath whenever you can. Two creatures carrying the reveal trigger is two reveals per damage step — four with double strike.
Going for the combo: Forerunner first, indestructibility up, then Polyraptor. Without protection, still go — eight Polyraptors with Terror of the Peaks or Wrathful Raptors out is usually enough.
Blasphemous Act is two different cards. With Wrathful Raptors out it is the kill; without it, only cast it when you are losing the board anyway.
